newsitem.title: USA: Dark lipstick sparks culture clash in Kentucky.
newsitem.headline: Dark lipstick sparks culture clash in Kentucky.

text.p: An eighth-grade girl who has insisted on her right to wear black lipstick despite being barred from school was sent home again Thursday, this time for wearing purple lipstick, authorities said.

"Some view this as a clash between traditional and modern values," Pike County School Board spokesman Bruce Hopkins said of the ongoing dispute over whether cosmetics constitute a distraction at an elementary school in this mountainous region bordering West Virginia.
"Personally I have no problem with black lipstick. It didn't bother me when I was a teacher," he said, adding that each school in the state can set its own standard for proper attire.

Karla Chapman, 13, was first suspended for three days from Runyon Elementary School in mid-November, and at a subsequent meeting between her parents and school principal Rosa Wolf, the principal accused the parents of threatening her. The parents vowed to keep their daughter out of school until the charge was dismissed. A trial date was set for February.
Hopkins said local news reports indicated the girl's mother said her daughter tried to commit suicide.
